passages.text: This is the burden of the word of the LORD against the land of Hadrach and Damascus its resting place— for the eyes of men and of all the tribes of Israel are upon the LORD — and also against Hamath, which borders it, as well as Tyre and Sidon, though they are very shrewd.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks a message against the land of Hadrach.
Damascus is the place where this message rests.
The LORD sees all people.
All the tribes of Israel look to the LORD.
The LORD also speaks against Hamath.
Hamath borders Hadrach.
The LORD speaks against Tyre and Sidon.
Tyre and Sidon are very wise.
passages.original: מַשָּׂ֤א דְבַר־ יְהוָה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חַדְרָ֔ךְ וְדַמֶּ֖שֶׂק מְנֻחָת֑וֹ כִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ עֵ֣ין אָדָ֔ם וְכֹ֖ל שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וְגַם־ חֲמָ֖ת תִּגְבָּל־ בָּ֑הּ צֹ֣ר וְצִיד֔וֹן כִּ֥י חָֽכְמָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: Tyre has built herself a fortress; she has heaped up silver like dust, and gold like the dirt of the streets.
passages.sermon:
Tyre is a city.
Tyre built a strong fortress for herself.
Tyre gathered much silver.
She gathered silver until it was like dust.
She gathered gold until it was like the dirt in the streets.
passages.original: וַתִּ֥בֶן צֹ֛ר מָצ֖וֹר לָ֑הּ וַתִּצְבָּר־ כֶּ֙סֶף֙ כֶּֽעָפָ֔ר וְחָר֖וּץ כְּטִ֥יט חוּצֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Behold, the Lord will impoverish her and cast her wealth into the sea, and she will be consumed by fire.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the subject.
The Lord will make Tyre poor.
The Lord will throw Tyre’s wealth into the sea.
Fire will destroy Tyre.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֤ה אֲדֹנָי֙ יֽוֹרִשֶׁ֔נָּה וְהִכָּ֥ה בַיָּ֖ם חֵילָ֑הּ וְהִ֖יא בָּאֵ֥שׁ תֵּאָכֵֽל׃

passages.text: Ashkelon will see and fear; Gaza will writhe in agony, as will Ekron, for her hope will wither. There will cease to be a king in Gaza, and Ashkelon will be uninhabited.
passages.sermon:
Ashkelon is a city of the Philistines.
Ashkelon will see what happens.
Ashkelon will become afraid.
Gaza is another city of the Philistines.
Gaza will suffer greatly.
Ekron is also a city of the Philistines.
Ekron will suffer too.
Ekron’s hope will disappear.
Gaza will lose its king.
Ashkelon will become empty.
No one will live in Ashkelon.
passages.original: תֵּרֶ֨א אַשְׁקְל֜וֹן וְתִירָ֗א וְעַזָּה֙ וְתָחִ֣יל מְאֹ֔ד וְעֶקְר֖וֹן כִּֽי־ הֹבִ֣ישׁ מֶבָּטָ֑הּ וְאָ֤בַד מֶ֙לֶךְ֙ מֵֽעַזָּ֔ה וְאַשְׁקְל֖וֹן לֹ֥א תֵשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: A mixed race will occupy Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
passages.sermon: God will act against the Philistines.\r\nA mixed people will live in Ashdod.\r\nGod will remove the pride of the Philistines.
passages.original: וְיָשַׁ֥ב מַמְזֵ֖ר בְּאַשְׁדּ֑וֹד וְהִכְרַתִּ֖י גְּא֥וֹן פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

passages.text: I will remove the blood from their mouths and the abominations from between their teeth. Then they too will become a remnant for our God; they will become like a clan in Judah, and Ekron will be like the Jebusites.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the Philistines.
God will act.
God will remove the blood from their mouths.
God will take away the abominations from between their teeth.
Some Philistines will remain for God.
They will belong to God.
They will become like a clan in Judah.
Ekron will become like the Jebusites.
passages.original: וַהֲסִרֹתִ֨י דָמָ֜יו מִפִּ֗יו וְשִׁקֻּצָיו֙ מִבֵּ֣ין שִׁנָּ֔יו וְנִשְׁאַ֥ר גַּם־ ה֖וּא לֵֽאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְהָיָה֙ כְּאַלֻּ֣ף בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְעֶקְר֖וֹן כִּיבוּסִֽי׃

passages.text: But I will camp around My house because of an army, because of those who march to and fro, and never again will an oppressor overrun My people, for now I keep watch with My own eyes.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God promises to protect His house.
God says, “I will camp around My house.”
God does this because of an army.
God does this because of those who march back and forth.
God says, “No oppressor will ever overrun My people again.”
God says, “Now I keep watch with My own eyes.”
passages.original: וְחָנִ֨יתִי לְבֵיתִ֤י מִצָּבָה֙ מֵעֹבֵ֣ר וּמִשָּׁ֔ב וְלֹֽא־ יַעֲבֹ֧ר עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם ע֖וֹד נֹגֵ֑שׂ כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה רָאִ֥יתִי בְעֵינָֽי׃ס

passages.text: Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion! Shout in triumph, O Daughter of Jerusalem! See, your King comes to you, righteous and victorious, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
passages.sermon:
Daughter of Zion, rejoice greatly.
Daughter of Jerusalem, shout in triumph.
Your King is coming to you.
He is righteous.
He is victorious.
He is humble.
He rides on a donkey.
He rides on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
passages.original: גִּילִ֨י מְאֹ֜ד בַּת־ צִיּ֗וֹן הָרִ֙יעִי֙ בַּ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם הִנֵּ֤ה מַלְכֵּךְ֙ יָ֣בוֹא לָ֔ךְ צַדִּ֥יק וְנוֹשָׁ֖ע ה֑וּא עָנִי֙ וְרֹכֵ֣ב עַל־ חֲמ֔וֹר וְעַל־ עַ֖יִר בֶּן־ אֲתֹנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem, and the bow of war will be broken. Then He will proclaim peace to the nations. His dominion will extend from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth.
passages.sermon:
God will act with power.
God will remove the chariot from Ephraim.
God will take away the horse from Jerusalem.
God will break the bow used for war.
God will end instruments of battle.
The King will speak peace to the nations.
The King will bring a message of peace to all peoples.
The King's rule will reach from sea to sea.
The King's authority will stretch from the Euphrates River to the ends of the earth.
passages.original: וְהִכְרַתִּי־ רֶ֣כֶב מֵאֶפְרַ֗יִם וְסוּס֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְנִכְרְתָה֙ קֶ֣שֶׁת מִלְחָמָ֔ה וְדִבֶּ֥ר שָׁל֖וֹם לַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּמָשְׁלוֹ֙ מִיָּ֣ם עַד־ יָ֔ם וּמִנָּהָ֖ר עַד־ אַפְסֵי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: As for you, because of the blood of My covenant, I will release your prisoners from the waterless pit.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God made a covenant with them.
This covenant was sealed with blood.
Because of this covenant, God acts.
God will set their prisoners free.
These prisoners are trapped in a pit.
This pit has no water.
God will release them from this dry pit.
passages.original: גַּם־ אַ֣תְּ בְּדַם־ בְּרִיתֵ֗ךְ שִׁלַּ֤חְתִּי אֲסִירַ֙יִךְ֙ מִבּ֔וֹר אֵ֥ין מַ֖יִם בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Return to your stronghold, O prisoners of hope; even today I declare that I will restore to you double.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people who are prisoners of hope.
He calls them to return to their stronghold.
God promises them restoration.
He declares this promise today.
God will give them back double what they lost.
passages.original: שׁ֚וּבוּ לְבִצָּר֔וֹן אֲסִירֵ֖י הַתִּקְוָ֑ה גַּם־ הַיּ֕וֹם מַגִּ֥יד מִשְׁנֶ֖ה אָשִׁ֥יב לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: For I will bend Judah as My bow and fit it with Ephraim. I will rouse your sons, O Zion, against the sons of Greece. I will make you like the sword of a mighty man.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God uses Judah as His bow.
God fits Ephraim as the arrow in this bow.
God stirs up the sons of Zion.
God moves the sons of Zion to rise against the sons of Greece.
God makes Zion strong.
God makes Zion like the sword of a mighty man.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ דָרַ֨כְתִּי לִ֜י יְהוּדָ֗ה קֶ֚שֶׁת מִלֵּ֣אתִי אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְעוֹרַרְתִּ֤י בָנַ֙יִךְ֙ צִיּ֔וֹן עַל־ בָּנַ֖יִךְ יָוָ֑ן וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךְ כְּחֶ֥רֶב גִּבּֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Then the LORD will appear over them, and His arrow will go forth like lightning. The Lord GOD will sound the ram’s horn and advance in the whirlwinds of the south.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
\r\nThe LORD will appear over His people.
\r\nThe LORD will show Himself to them.
\r\nThe LORD will send out His arrow.
\r\nHis arrow will go out like lightning.
\r\nThe Lord GOD will sound the ram’s horn.
\r\nThe Lord GOD will move forward.
\r\nHe will advance in the whirlwinds of the south.
passages.original: וַֽיהוָה֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם יֵֽרָאֶ֔ה וְיָצָ֥א כַבָּרָ֖ק חִצּ֑וֹ וַֽאדֹנָ֤י יְהֹוִה֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֣ר יִתְקָ֔ע וְהָלַ֖ךְ בְּסַעֲר֥וֹת תֵּימָֽן׃

passages.text: The LORD of Hosts will shield them. They will destroy and conquer with slingstones; they will drink and roar as with wine. And they will be filled like sprinkling bowls, drenched like the corners of the altar.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts will protect His people.
He will shield them from harm.
They will destroy their enemies with slingstones.
They will conquer those who oppose them.
They will drink and make noise like people who have drunk wine.
They will be filled up like bowls used for sprinkling.
They will be drenched like the corners of the altar.
passages.original: יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֮ יָגֵ֣ן עֲלֵיהֶם֒ וְאָכְל֗וּ וְכָֽבְשׁוּ֙ אַבְנֵי־ קֶ֔לַע וְשָׁת֥וּ הָמ֖וּ כְּמוֹ־ יָ֑יִן וּמָֽלְאוּ֙ כַּמִּזְרָ֔ק כְּזָוִיּ֖וֹת מִזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: On that day the LORD their God will save them as the flock of His people; for like jewels in a crown they will sparkle over His land.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is their God.
He will save His people on that day.
He will save them like a shepherd saves his flock.
His people are like sheep.
They belong to Him.
They will shine in His land.
They will shine like jewels in a crown.
passages.original: וְֽהוֹשִׁיעָ֞ם יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כְּצֹ֣אן עַמּ֑וֹ כִּ֚י אַבְנֵי־ נֵ֔זֶר מִֽתְנוֹסְס֖וֹת עַל־ אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: How lovely they will be, and how beautiful! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine, the young women.
passages.sermon:
The LORD cares for His people.
He blesses them with goodness and beauty.
The young men will grow strong because of grain.
The young women will thrive because of new wine.
passages.original: כִּ֥י מַה־ טּוּב֖וֹ וּמַה־ יָפְי֑וֹ דָּגָן֙ בַּֽחוּרִ֔ים וְתִיר֖וֹשׁ יְנוֹבֵ֥ב בְּתֻלֽוֹת׃
